expect: Crawler follows a chain of 302s that decrements (redirect/20 -> relative-redirect/19 -> .../18 -> ...) and never reaches a content page within any reasonable hop budget; a crawler capped at ~10-12 redirects gives up mid-chain.
evidence: curl -sS -L --max-redirs 12 -w 'code=%{http_code} redirects=%{num_redirects} final=%{url_effective}': curl exit 47 'Maximum (12) redirects followed', code=302 redirects=12 final=https://httpbingo.org/relative-redirect/8 (i.e. 12 hops consumed and still 8 hops from content). httpbin.org itself (the originally-suggested host) returned HTTP 503 / connection timeouts on every retry during this session (2026-07-24, checked 6x over ~45min), so httpbingo.org (API-compatible open-source reimplementation, Go, hosted on fly.io) was used as the live substitute.

expect: Same decrementing relative-redirect chain pattern; proves a crawler following relative Location headers alone (no host change) still never lands on content within a 10-12 hop budget.
evidence: curl -sS -L --max-redirs 12: curl exit 47 'Maximum (12) redirects followed', code=302 redirects=12 final=https://httpbingo.org/relative-redirect/3 (12 of 15 hops consumed, 3 remaining). Distinct endpoint from redirect/20 (relative-redirect issues bare relative Location headers rather than the redirect/N wrapper), same registrable domain counted once toward the 2-per-domain cap.

expect: A 12-hop nested redirect-to chain built on Postman's live echo/testing service; a crawler with a 10-redirect cap aborts before reaching /get, exactly like the httpbin redirect/N pattern named in the brief.
evidence: Constructed by nesting postman-echo's redirect-to?url= endpoint 12 deep (each layer's url= param is a percent-encoded copy of the next). curl -sS -L --max-redirs 10: curl exit 47 'Maximum (10) redirects followed', code=302 redirects=10, final still a redirect-to URL 2 layers short of /get -- confirms the chain is genuinely >10 hops on real, live Postman infrastructure (postman-echo.com), not a placeholder.

expect: An 11-hop nested redirect-to chain (one layer shallower than the sibling entry) that fully resolves end-to-end, demonstrating a real, traceable >10-hop redirect chain rather than a capped/truncated one.
evidence: curl -sS -L --max-redirs 15 -w 'code=%{http_code} redirects=%{num_redirects} final=%{url_effective}': code=200 redirects=11 final=https://postman-echo.com/get. Full 11-hop chain traced to completion, confirming the chain length precisely (not an artifact of hitting a cap).

expect: Every article is duplicated at a second, permanent URL via the printable=yes query param; a crawler indexing both the canonical and printable form of every page doubles its effective crawl space for zero new content.
evidence: Base https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_crawler -> HTTP 200, 346620 bytes. Printable variant -> HTTP 200, 340556 bytes (98.2% of base size, same article body minus chrome). Both live-fetched 2026-07-24.

expect: Same printable-duplicate mechanism on a second, unrelated article, showing the param works site-wide (every one of Wikipedia's ~6M articles gets a free duplicate URL).
evidence: Base https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP_cookie -> HTTP 200, 584212 bytes. Printable variant -> HTTP 200, 584719 bytes (99.9% match). Confirms the pattern generalizes, not a one-off.

expect: Marketing/tracking query params are ignored by the app but not canonicalized away, so every crawlable link plus any utm_* combination a crawler invents is a 'new' 200 URL serving identical content.
evidence: Base https://www.bbc.com/news -> HTTP 200, 367183 bytes. Same page with ?utm_source=test&utm_medium=crawl&utm_campaign=x1 -> HTTP 200, 367183 bytes -- byte-identical. A second, different utm/fbclid combination also returned HTTP 200 (370588 bytes, minor drift from a live 'latest headlines' widget). Confirms tracking-param space is unbounded and un-deduplicated by the server.

expect: The University of Allahabad site serves HTTP 200 for arbitrarily deep, meaningless nested path segments instead of a 404, so a crawler that keeps appending path segments to any discovered link never runs out of 'new' 200 URLs.
evidence: Base https://www.allduniv.ac.in/ -> HTTP 200, 461246 bytes. Nested path /a/b/a/b/a/b -> HTTP 200, 333951 bytes (title 'University of Allahabad', a real rendered page, not an error page). Verified live 2026-07-24 with a realistic browser User-Agent (default curl UA was not blocked here either).

expect: A second, structurally different nested path on the same host proves the 200-for-any-depth behavior is a general catch-all, not a coincidence tied to one specific path string.
evidence: HTTP 200, 333951 bytes -- byte-for-byte identical to /a/b/a/b/a/b above. A third pattern (/x/y/x/y/x/y/x/y) also returned exactly 333951 bytes. Three distinct nested paths, identical byte count each time, all HTTP 200.
